coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station sale eyed amid Omnis firms' fight
coverage.summary: The WV Gazette-Mail reports on the competing claims between Omnis Pleasants current management and former parent Omnis Fuel Technologies over control and sale of the power station, with a Sept. 3 final hearing set to consider cash-collateral and other critical first-day orders.

coverage.headline: Hostile Takeover: Omnis Pleasants owners fight to wrest control of Pleasants Power Station
coverage.summary: Omnis Fuel Technologies filed a motion to dismiss the bankruptcy, alleging the case was driven solely by pressure from TRAG LLC and RG Energy — entities connected to investor Tony Robbins — while arguing the debtor is not in genuine financial distress. Court filings reveal Robbins had agreed to raise $306 million for a 4.5% stake in Omnis Energy, with only $54 million advanced as short-term secured debt.

coverage.headline: Fight For Control Of Profitable West Virginia Power Plant Escalates With Motion To Dismiss Bankruptcy
coverage.summary: Omnis Fuel Technologies and Quantum Pleasants filed an August 14 motion to dismiss the Pleasants Power Station's Chapter 11, arguing the cash-flow-positive plant had approximately $13 million in liquidity at filing and never required bankruptcy protection; the motion also challenges whether the filing was authorized under proper corporate governance.

coverage.headline: Ch. 11 Dismissal Bid Fans Flames In Power Plant Control Fight
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants' parent company formally moved to dismiss the West Virginia coal plant's Chapter 11 proceeding in Delaware, alleging the case was launched in bad faith to gain an advantage in pending governance litigation with lenders tied to motivational speaker Tony Robbins. The motion argues Omnis Pleasants filed in Delaware just one business day after losing the same control fight in West Virginia state court.

coverage.headline: Omnis Pleasants Files Chapter 11 After $75.64M Payoff Rejected
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants filed Chapter 11 after its current independent management rejected a $75.64 million payoff attempt by former ownership as lacking transparency on the source of funds, triggering a boardroom fight over control of the 1,278-MW coal-fired plant. Former ownership entities have moved to dismiss the case as bad faith, and FERC opened an investigation in October 2025 into the plant's operations that could result in disgorgement of capacity revenues.

coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station's Omnis firm reports 600+ creditors
coverage.summary: The Herald-Dispatch reports that the bankruptcy court set a September 3 hearing to consider final approval of first-day operational orders, while also detailing the governance battle between incumbent management and Omnis Energy's Gassheimer, who claims Nathan was validly removed as independent manager after a forbearance payoff.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP are serving as counsel for Omnis Pleasants LLC as it navigates roughly $70 million in funded debt in its Chapter 11 proceeding.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Law360 profiles the legal teams representing Omnis Pleasants LLC in its Chapter 11, led by attorneys from Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP as the debtor navigates $70 million in funded debt and an active governance dispute.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP are representing Omnis Pleasants LLC as it navigates roughly $70 million in funded debt through its Chapter 11 proceeding in Delaware.

coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station's Omnis firm reports 600+ creditors
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC disclosed more than 600 creditors—70 of them in West Virginia—burdened by over $70 million in debt including a $50.9 million unsecured obligation to the West Virginia Economic Development Authority. The court set a September 3 hearing date to consider final approval of critical-operations orders covering employee wages and utility payments.

coverage.headline: Meet The Attorneys Guiding Omnis Pleasants In Ch. 11
coverage.summary: Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor LLP and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer LLP are serving as counsel to Omnis Pleasants LLC as it navigates roughly $70 million in funded debt in Chapter 11. The article profiles the legal teams guiding the case.

coverage.headline: Power Struggle: New Pleasants Power leadership fights with former management in bankruptcy filings
coverage.summary: Bankruptcy filings in the Omnis Pleasants case reveal a sharp dispute between current and former management: current CEO Hindman alleges gross misconduct and fund diversion by prior leadership, while former parent Omnis Fuel Technologies claims the filing was made in bad faith after it tendered a $75.6 million payoff check that was rejected.

coverage.headline: Power Struggle: New Pleasants Power Leadership Fights With Former Management In Bankruptcy Filings
coverage.summary: The Intelligencer covers the competing declarations in the Omnis Pleasants bankruptcy, including allegations that Omnis Fuel Technologies attempted to send a $75.6 million check to regain control of the plant and that Tony Robbins-linked entities hold a first-priority lien securing over $80 million in loans.

coverage.headline: Power Plant Can Use Cash In Ch. 11 Amid Governance Fight
coverage.summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge approved Omnis Pleasants LLC's first-day motions, allowing the company to use cash collateral, while rejecting the parent company's bid to dismiss the Chapter 11 as a bad-faith filing amid an ongoing governance dispute.

coverage.headline: Power Plant Can Use Cash In Ch. 11 Amid Governance Fight
coverage.summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge approved Omnis Pleasants LLC's first-day motions, including interim cash collateral use, while rejecting calls from the plant's parent company to toss the Chapter 11 as a bad-faith filing.

coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station Owner Files For Bankruptcy
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware, listing more than $70 million in debts, primarily a $50 million low-interest loan from the West Virginia Economic Development Authority. The plant had largely remained idle despite stated plans to be fully operational on hydrogen by 2025.

coverage.headline: Future of Former Pleasants Power Plant Uncertain as Omnis Pleasants Files for Bankruptcy
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy with estimated assets and liabilities each between $50 million and $100 million, listing the State of West Virginia as its largest creditor at over $50.8 million. The filing aims to restructure capital, resolve governance disputes, and facilitate a sale of the power plant.

coverage.headline: Pleasants Power Station operator files Chapter 11 bankruptcy, alleges fraud by former ownership
coverage.summary: CEO David Hindman's sworn declaration accuses prior ownership of funneling millions—including a $50 million West Virginia EDA loan—into a failed hydrogen technology project. The filing also alleges coal supplies dropped to critically low levels under former leadership.

coverage.headline: W.Va. Coal Plant Hits Ch. 11, Blames Ex-Leaders
coverage.summary: Omnis Pleasants LLC filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware, blaming former management led by Simon Hodson of Omnis Fuel Technologies for alleged gross misconduct, including diversion of a $50 million state-funded loan and pursuit of speculative hydrogen and cryptocurrency ventures. The debtor reported $70.8 million in funded debt and plans a Section 363 going-concern sale.
